purpose: Defines ordinary public applicability traits referenced by Adaptive Research nodes. Traits describe biological/civilizational capabilities or constraints; they are not playable-race IDs.

traits.name: Metabolic Biology
traits.description: The relevant population is biological and depends on metabolism, biochemical homeostasis, nutrition, and biological health systems.
traits.research_effect: Enables ordinary biological medicine, life-support, agriculture, biotechnology, and other metabolic-organism research where applicable.

traits.name: Gravity-Sensitive Biology
traits.description: Long-term health or development changes materially with sustained acceleration/gravity environment.
traits.research_effect: Allows high/low-gravity health and adaptation branches to emerge when real gravity mismatch exists.

traits.name: Heritable Genetic System
traits.description: Biological traits are encoded in a heritable information system that can eventually be deliberately modified with sufficient understanding.
traits.research_effect: Enables heritable biological engineering and long-term directed adaptation.

traits.name: Metabolic Suppression Physiology
traits.description: The species' physiology can plausibly tolerate a deliberately induced low-metabolism state after adequate medical development. This can be innate or become possible after precursor biological engineering.
traits.research_effect: Makes induced torpor a viable implementation of long-duration habitation.

traits.name: Machine Cognition Present
traits.description: The civilization contains autonomous machine/synthetic cognition sophisticated enough to exist as persistent agents, institutions, or populations.
traits.research_effect: Enables synthetic-civilization survival, identity, habitat, replication, and machine-population research. A biological civilization can gain this trait through its own technological history.

traits.name: Biological Fabrication Capability
traits.description: The civilization has developed biological manufacturing capable of deliberately growing or assembling engineered structural/industrial material rather than merely modifying organisms for medicine or agriculture.
traits.research_effect: Allows living-material and living-vehicle branches to emerge after enabling biotechnology is actually mastered, even for a species that did not begin with biological fabrication traditions.
